title: Slave Trade and Urban Slavery on the Swahili Coast from Medieval Times to Abolition
locator: Abstract and medieval c.750-1500 synthesis; steady but not massive export; dependence complexity
claim_fitness: Strong for persistent medieval slave-trade participation and for constraining scale/uniformity; not port-by-port exact-1400 evidence
access_limitation: Publisher abstract and structured chapter summary read; full paywalled chapter not exhaustively reread
dependency_note: Interpretive backbone; synthesizes earlier primary and secondary traditions and is not counted as a new independent event

title: When Did the Swahili Become Maritime?
locator: Discussion of Rasulid Yemen customs, late-14th-century Qadi Masud, regular voyages and eastern African commodities including slaves
claim_fitness: Strong for regular thirteenth/fourteenth-century East Africa-Arabia maritime structure with slaves among traded commodities; unfit to prove every Swahili node or cargo carried slaves
access_limitation: Open/searchable article text used; underlying customs editions/Vallet 2010 not independently reconstructed
dependency_note: Specific customs claims depend partly on Rasulid/Yemeni source scholarship including Vallet; preserve that dependency

title: Ibn Battuta on slaves at Kilwa
locator: Kilwa 1331; ruler raids Zanj country; twenty enslaved people given in court episode
claim_fitness: Strong for enslaved presence/transfer at Kilwa and for reported ruler raiding; does not establish coast-wide prevalence or slave-export volume
access_limitation: Modern English translation/reproduction read; Arabic text not independently edited in this pass
dependency_note: Teaching page and Freeman-Grenville translation are one Ibn Battuta textual chain, not independent witnesses

title: No such thing as invisible people: toward an archaeology of slavery at the fifteenth-century Swahili site of Songo Mnara
locator: Fifteenth-century Songo Mnara; terracotta/shell beads and domestic/productive contexts as possible enslaved/underclass proxies
claim_fitness: Strong bounded specialist interpretation for likely enslaved workers at Songo Mnara; material proxies are ambiguous and do not quantify or generalize prevalence
access_limitation: Open-access full text read; proxy-status ambiguity explicitly preserved
dependency_note: Already represented in repository site case; reuse is dependency-aware and not counted as a new independent discovery

title: Traces of Clay: Exploring Slave and Migrant Identities in Medieval Swahili Zanzibar
locator: Tumbatu/Mkokotoni c.1000-1400; outlier pottery; medieval slavery/migration discussion; explicit scale and status limits
claim_fitness: Useful for c.1400 archaeological context and for distinguishing enslaved people from migrants/dependents; does not prove slave status of individual potters or quantify scale
access_limitation: Open-access Cambridge article read; broad historical discussion partly depends on Vernet and Rødland et al. 2020
dependency_note: Separate site dataset but interpretive background overlaps earlier Swahili slavery scholarship; do not double-count broad claims

title: Ifugao Law
locator: Slaves section pp.35-36; child sale; ownership/inheritance; debt servitude; captives sold for debt
claim_fitness: Strong for serious unfreedom in later traditional Ifugao society; unfit to date those institutions to exact 1700 without independent continuity evidence
access_limitation: Colonial-era English ethnography; retrospective temporal reach is broad and partly unspecified
dependency_note: Same fieldwork/tradition as Barton 1922; count as one principal evidence family

title: Ifugao Economics
locator: Servants and Slaves; himbut; child sale/debt bonding; manumission/incorporation
claim_fitness: Strong for source-native himbut category and varied servile outcomes; unfit for exact-1700 dating and not independent from Barton 1919
access_limitation: Digitized text read; colonial-era terminology and retrospective framing require caution
dependency_note: Related Barton ethnographic programme; category variation within same evidence family

title: Class Structure in the Unhispanized Philippines
locator: Ifugao petty-plutocracy/propertyless/debt-peon discussion; comparative chattel-slave distinction
claim_fitness: Important caution against treating every Ifugao dependent/propertyless status as chattel slavery; does not erase Barton but narrows category translation
access_limitation: Publisher metadata plus searchable article reproduction consulted; exact source traditions synthesized by Scott not exhaustively reconstructed
dependency_note: Independent later comparative interpretation; use as category challenge, not absence evidence

title: Ifugao Archaeology: Collaborative and Indigenous Archaeology in the Northern Philippines
locator: Archaeological models; Spanish encounter mid-1600s; first written description 1793; colonial/pericolonial transformation
claim_fitness: Strong for seventeenth/eighteenth-century chronology and for showing the written-source gap near 1700; no slave-status attestation
access_limitation: Open publisher text read; archaeology is local/project-specific and does not cover every Ifugao community
dependency_note: Same modern IAP research programme as Acabado et al. 2019; not independent evidence of slavery

title: The Short History of the Ifugao Rice Terraces: A Local Response to the Spanish Conquest
locator: Old Kiyyangan/terrace chronology; social and agricultural change after c.1600
claim_fitness: Strong for social/agricultural transformation around the anchor; unfit to infer slavery from hierarchy, labor mobilization or intensification
access_limitation: Publisher abstract/project synthesis used; no slave-status diagnostic claimed
dependency_note: Same IAP programme as Acabado 2017; contextual exact-period evidence only
